summary: Quarterly business review focused on usage trends, cost optimization opportunities, reliability incidents and roadmap alignment. Orion is running a mix of hosted API for dev and a small private deployment for PHI-sensitive workflows. Main asks: reduce token costs via batching/caching, confirm 99th pct latency under 350ms for 2k context, and get security/compliance artifacts for procurement. Agreed next steps include a performance benchmark and updated cost spreadsheet.
transcript:
[00:00] Sam Carter: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick roll call  Sam here from Redwood, Priya and Diego with me. Marta, Rahul, Leah, you there?
[00:10] Marta Liu: Yep hi, thanks. Sorry a little late ran over with an exec meeting.
[00:15] Rahul Singh: Rahul here.
[00:17] Leah Kim: Leah  good to see you all.
[00:20] Sam Carter: Great. The plan for today: quick Q1 usage review, walk through cost levers we recommended, cover reliability incidents, and then next steps for the pilot. Priya you want to kick off with adoption numbers?
[00:30] Priya Nair: Yeah sure. So quick snapshot, total tokens this quarter ~3.2B generated, embeddings about 120k units. Most of the growth was in the patient triage feature  that's about 58% of calls. Dev environment still on hosted API, private cluster handles PHI batch jobs. Monthly spend up 14% q/q, mostly from increased prompt lengths.
[00:50] Marta Liu: Just to clarify, the triage flows increased context to 6k in a few tests, that explains some of the spike. We didn't realize the token growth would be that sensitive.
[01:00] Diego Ramos: Right  longer context means KV cache miss rate goes up, which increases upstream compute. We had suggested prefix caching and more aggressive chunking in the triage prompt. I can share an example config.
[01:12] Leah Kim: When you say prefix caching, is that safe with PHI data? We have to be careful about retention.
[01:18] Priya Nair: Good call  we recommended cache keys that respect PII redaction and retention TTLs. For private deployment you can configure separate cache buckets with shorter TTLs or disable caching for PHI flows.
[01:30] Marta Liu: So is that a config change or do we need to rework prompts?
[01:35] Diego Ramos: Mostly config + minor prompt rewrite. We'll send a template.
[01:38] Sam Carter: On the cost side we modeled two levers: improved batching plus quantization on the private model variants. If you move higher-volume routes to a ded-committed pool we can cut unit cost by ~28% in our estimate.
[01:50] Rahul Singh: When you say ded-committed, you mean Redwood Dedicated? We've had some concerns about isolation and network egress.
[01:57] Sam Carter: Yes Dedicated  reserved GPU pools. Isolation is one of the main benefits. For network egress you can use VPC peering and private links, and for on-prem we have an air-gapped option. We'll include a diagram.
[02:10] Marta Liu: Any ballpark for 99th percentile latency at 2k vs 8k context on Dedicated? Our SLA target for triage is 350ms 99th.
[02:20] Diego Ramos: On similar gen-based models, with optimized kernels and batching, Dedicated on A100 equivalent can hit ~250300ms 99th at 2k with continuous batching. 8k context is trickier  99th gets to ~600800ms unless we use quantized model variants and kernel fusions. We can run a benchmark against your dataset to get exact numbers.
[02:40] Leah Kim: What about failover? If Dedicated has capacity issues, will it route to hosted and how will that affect data residency?
[02:48] Sam Carter: Smart routing can fail over to compatible model variants in the same region, but for PHI you can restrict fallback. We recommend canary + fallback policies that respect data class.
[02:58] Marta Liu: We also have procurement in the loop; they asked for SOC 2 and KMS details. Can you send certs?
[03:04] Priya Nair: Yes we'll share SOC 2 and KMS integration docs. For private deployments we have HSM options.
[03:10] Rahul Singh: On incidents, we had two spikes in Feb where token latency doubled for about 12 minutes. I can share our pager logs. Was that on your side?
[03:19] Diego Ramos: We saw a transient autoscaling delay in the EU region that correlated. I'm pulling the incident notes now  looks like a mis-sized autoscaler threshold. We patched it and added an override.
[03:30] Rahul Singh: Ok please share the RCA.
[03:33] Diego Ramos: Will do.
[03:34] Sam Carter: Back to cost  we recommended a mixed approach: keep hosted for dev and low-volume interactive routes, Dedicated for high-throughput triage, and Private for PHI. That gives you a balance of latency and compliance.
[03:46] Marta Liu: How painful is migration? We have around 30k queries/day for triage now.
[03:52] Diego Ramos: Migration is small-bore: model pinning, route-based traffic shift and test harness. For a pilot we typically do a heel-toe rollout over 24 weeks. We can also run shadow traffic to measure tail latency without impacting users.
[04:05] Leah Kim: Budget team will want updated cost savings. Can you produce a 12-month projection showing break-even vs hosted?
[04:12] Sam Carter: Yes  Sam here  we'll produce a 12-month TCO model including reserved commit tiers and expected savings from batching and quantization. That will be in the spreadsheet.
[04:20] Marta Liu: On quality, we saw a slight regression after quantizing one variant in January  responses were slightly less coherent for edge prompts. Any guardrails?
[04:29] Diego Ramos: We run evals against your prompt sets; we'll tie regression alerts to those evals and keep a non-quantized fallback for critical routes. There's a small tradeoff but usually acceptable after tuning.
[04:40] Rahul Singh: For the benchmark Diego mentioned, what infra do you need from our side?
[04:45] Diego Ramos: Ideally a redacted sample dataset, representative latencies, and a route definition. We'll run tests in your Dedicated region or on a staging private cluster if you prefer.
[04:55] Marta Liu: We can share a redacted triage log and a sample payload. I'll ask Rahul to gather logs.
[05:00] Rahul Singh: We'll sanitize and share by Friday.
[05:04] Priya Nair: On security docs  we'll attach the SOC2 report and the KMS/HSM integration guide. Note: for Private deployments there's an extra checklist around network and key rotation.
[05:14] Leah Kim: Procurement asked about support SLAs  what's the difference between standard and enterprise?
[05:19] Sam Carter: Standard support is business hours with 24-hour response for Sev 1. Enterprise provides 24/7 with faster response targets and an assigned TAM. We'll include the support matrix in the follow-up.
[05:29] Marta Liu: One more thing  our product roadmap wants to push embeddings for search in Q2; what's the recommended pattern to reduce cost?
[05:37] Diego Ramos: Use batched incremental embeddings and a deduplicated cache. Also use lower-dim embeddings for retrieval then rerank with the larger model. That reduces compute and storage costs.
[05:48] Leah Kim: Great. Anything else on the roadmap alignment?
[05:51] Sam Carter: We'll map your Q2 goals to Redwood capabilities  pilot for Dedicated, private cluster readiness, and performance benchmark.
[05:58] Marta Liu: Sounds good. Let's recap next steps.
[06:01] Sam Carter: Recap: Sam sends cost model + usage CSV; Diego runs latency benchmarks; Priya sends security docs; Marta confirms pilot stakeholders; Rahul shares infra logs. We'll plan follow-up call once benchmarks are in.
[06:14] Marta Liu: Thanks all.
[06:16] Leah Kim: Thanks everyone.
[06:18] Sam Carter: Thanks  meeting adjourned.
